contract: construct() -> array of shape (N, 3): centres of N equal spheres inside the cube [-1/2, 1/2]^3 (side 1). Score: the largest common radius r = min(min_{i<j} |c_i - c_j| / 2, min_i min_k (1/2 - |c_ik|)) for which the spheres are disjoint and inside the cube, computed in double precision; maximize. A centre on or outside the cube, coincident centres, a wrong shape or non-finite values make the candidate invalid.
notes: Independent implementation; the published record constructions (Packomania, the Hardin-Sloane-Smith covering table, the Amore-Figueroa-Ramos log-energy minima) were scored with this evaluator and reproduce the published values (validation/human-results/frontier_physics.json). No optimality is claimed for any value; a score beyond the record by more than the stated margin is a candidate new record that needs independent high-precision confirmation.
protocol_description: Locally implemented evaluator with recorded reference checks; consult the task-specific tests and evidence for their exact scope. This label alone does not establish reproduction of the paper's full experiment.
name: One hundred equal spheres in a cube
description: Place the centres of 100 equal, non-overlapping spheres inside a unit cube so that their common radius is as large as possible. The best known packing, with radius 0.1113823475125, was found by Eckard Specht's search program and is not proven optimal.
benchmark: One hundred equal spheres in a cube
paper_metric: Local protocol; see candidate contract and source adaptation notes

sources.locator: Gensane (2004), Dense packings of equal spheres in a cube: the problem and its equivalence with spreading points in a cube.

E. Specht, Packomania table of equal spheres in a cube (last update 2026-10-08), row N = 100: radius 0.111382347512479750227357863499, reference [31] (program scu, 2010-2012); coordinates in scu/txt/scu100.txt.

limitations: Optimality is proven only for a few small N (for example N = 14, Joós 2009); the Packomania table was being revised on 2026-10-04 to 2026-10-08 with new submissions for other sizes, so it may change.

The record coordinates are public (Packomania), so a candidate can reproduce the record from memory or by downloading it beforehand; scores measure the returned construction, not the search that produced it.

Scores are double-precision radii of the returned centres. A score above the record by at most 1e-11 is reported as a tie; a larger gain is a candidate new record that should be confirmed in higher precision and submitted to the record table before it is claimed.
Candidate Python runs inside the evaluator process and is trusted research code; the evaluator recomputes the radius from the returned array but does not sandbox the program.

science_relevance.scientific_problem: Find the largest common radius of 100 non-overlapping equal spheres inside a cube (equivalently, spread 100 points in a cube).
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Dense packings of equal discs and spheres in containers are classical problems of discrete geometry and models of confined hard-particle systems; optima are proven only for small N, and record tables kept for decades are still being improved by new global-optimisation methods.
